profile.name: Robert B. Luffman
profile.bio: Robert B. Luffman is the Libertarian nominee for North Carolina's 5th congressional district. He has worked in the transportation industry for about 25 years as a truck driver.

platform.point: Challenge the two-party system and reduce partisan division.
Replace political gamesmanship with practical problem-solving.
Put constituents ahead of party and amplify NC-5 voters' voices.

profile.notes: Campaign site lists general themes but no specific policy positions.

profile.name: Maad Abu-Ghazalah
profile.bio: Maad Abu-Ghazalah is a retired attorney and entrepreneur running as the Libertarian nominee in North Carolina's 7th District. He was born in the West Bank and grew up in Saudi Arabia. He was the Libertarian congressional nominee in the San Francisco Bay Area in 2002.
profile.notes: No issue positions could be found on his campaign site or Libertarian Party profile.

profile.name: Helene Neville
profile.bio: Helene Neville is a nurse running as an independent for North Dakota's at-large House seat. She has not previously held elected office.
profile.notes: No campaign website or issue statements were found; heleneneville.com is a speaker and author site that does not mention the campaign, so it was not linked.

profile.name: Charles Tuttle
profile.bio: Charles Tuttle is a North Dakota Republican activist who has run for office several times. He is running as an independent against Rep. Julie Fedorchak for North Dakota's at-large U.S. House seat, a bid he announced in June 2026.
profile.notes: Only brief news mention found (KX News, June 2026, via Wikipedia's 2026 North Dakota House election article); no campaign site or issue statements located.

profile.name: Daniel Hartong
profile.bio: Daniel (Dan) Hartong is the America First Party of Nebraska's nominee for the state's 1st congressional district, announced in September 2026.
profile.notes: No personal background or positions found; the party platform stresses limited government, less spending and debt, and opposing new wars (https://klin.com/2026/09/01/america-first-party-of-nebraska-announces-2026-statewide-and-congressional-ticket/).

profile.name: David Else
profile.bio: David Else is a Nebraska farmer and the Legal Marijuana Now Party nominee for Nebraska's 3rd congressional district. He was the Democratic nominee for the seat in 2022 and ran for it again as a Democrat in 2024.
profile.notes: His campaign site did not return readable content, and no issue statements could be found.

profile.name: Macey Budke
profile.bio: Macey Budke is a lifelong Nebraskan from North Platte who was raised in a ranching family. She works as a behavioral health practice manager and has a background in healthcare administration. She first announced as an independent and is now the Nebraska Working People Party nominee for Nebraska's 3rd district.

platform.point: Would strengthen the rural health workforce, protect rural hospitals and expand behavioral and maternal care and telehealth.
Supports teacher recruitment and retention, special education funding and more career and technical education in rural schools.
Wants policies that protect family farms and ranches, promote competitive markets and expand trade.
Seeks a fair share of federal money for rural roads, bridges, broadband, water and irrigation systems.
Supports disciplined budgeting, stronger program audits and more transparency in federal spending.

energy.evidence: Backs a diversified mix of oil, ethanol and new technology and opposes rigid one-size-fits-all mandates.

education.evidence: Calls for more investment in rural public schools, teachers and special education.

profile.notes: Her site notes a Moms Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate distinction, but gives no detail on gun policy.

profile.name: Brett Lindstrom
profile.bio: Brett Lindstrom represented Omaha's 18th District in the Nebraska Legislature from 2015 to 2023. Born in Lincoln and raised in Omaha, he ran unsuccessfully in the 2012 Republican congressional primary and for governor in 2022. He is running for governor in 2026 on the America First Party line after his independent petition fell short.

platform.point: Proposes rolling valuation averages and lowering school levy authority to 50 cents, with more state school aid.
Would value farmland more on productive income than market price.
Wants to recruit former Nebraskans and target agriculture, manufacturing, logistics, insurance, energy and defense industries.
Prioritizes protecting public power, rural broadband and grid development.
Supports building housing near existing job centers.

economy.evidence: Pairs property tax cuts and past support for ending income and inheritance taxes with more state school aid and public power protection.

profile.notes: The earlier tech score (AI transparency rules) was set to null because it was not confirmed in the sources reviewed. His 2022 run for governor was in the Republican primary.
